daq_query.description: Query historical/live data for DAQ nodes you can access. Access is granted either by direct node binding or by the channel's line binding (read-only for all DAQ nodes on that line). Filters: line/product/recipe/run/time window/downsampling (product and recipe filters use per-sample tags, so a specific batch can be selected precisely). Results carry physical meaning (semantics, unit, range, statistics, recent series). By default only the **current active batch (active recipe)** is queried; pass scope=all explicitly to compare across recipes or review full history.

node_id.description: Restrict to one DAQ node id (default: all bound nodes)

product_id.description: Filter by product (per-sample tags); passing it overrides the default active-batch filter

recipe_id.description: Filter by recipe (per-sample tags); passing it overrides the default filter. Default: the active recipe of the node's line (no filter if the line is not running)

run_id.description: Filter by run id (pin one run when a recipe was started multiple times); passing it overrides the default filter

scope.description: Scope: active (default) = current active batch only; all = no recipe filter, return every sample in the window (cross-recipe comparison/history review)

from_ms.description: Start epoch ms (paired with to_ms; takes precedence over last_minutes)

bucket_ms.description: Downsampling bucket width in ms (default {queryDefaultBucketMs}, floor {queryMinBucketMs})

recipe_catalog.description: List recipe definitions on lines you can read (find recipe_id / the currently running recipe / product ownership). Each entry includes recipe id, version, product, whether it is running, parameter count, each node's target and PLC value, and last good batch. Supports line_id/product_id/keyword filters. Use this first when unsure of a recipe_id; recipe_apply/recipe_trial/recipe_update can also take line_id and resolve the active recipe. Read-only.

line_id.description: Restrict to a line id (must be readable)

recipe_update.description: Save verified best parameters into a recipe as a new version with attribution and rationale. You may target the currently running recipe by passing only line_id (resolved from the active batch), or pass recipe_id explicitly. Permission model: you must be bound to the recipe (multiple bindings allowed) and pass its secondary auth; the recipe must be running (run gate). With a manual binding or manual line, the save suspends for human approval — reason is required and must cite evidence (DAQ data/analysis); the approval card shows it. This changes the definition only; use recipe_apply to push parameters to the running line.

recipe_id.description: Recipe id (mutually exclusive with line_id; explicit id wins)

params.description: Parameters to update (partial merge; list only nodes that change)

node_id.description: DCW node id (must be one of your bound DCW nodes)

min.description: Optional new recipe window lower bound

max.description: Optional new recipe window upper bound

reason.description: Why this change is saved (required; state the evidence)

line_id.description: Line id (mutually exclusive with recipe_id): resolve the recipe from that line's active batch

recipe_apply.description: Dispatch the recipe's currently persisted parameters to the running line as one batch (use after recipe_update). You may target the running recipe with only line_id (resolved from the active batch) or pass recipe_id explicitly. Permission model: bound recipe, secondary auth, and run gate (recipe must be executing). With a manual binding or manual line, dispatch suspends for human approval — reason is required and must explain why and on what evidence. After approval the batch goes through governance interlocks (range/step/rate) with per-parameter acknowledgements. A rejection may include guidance; revise and resubmit.

recipe_id.description: Recipe id (mutually exclusive with line_id; explicit id wins)

reason.description: Why dispatch (required): data evidence/trial conclusion/goal-gap analysis; the line expert must understand your reasoning on the approval card

emergency.description: Emergency exemption from the recipe dispatch rate limit (does NOT skip approval; the card is marked [EMERGENCY] and still needs a human; abuse is audited)

line_id.description: Line id (mutually exclusive with recipe_id): resolve the recipe from the active batch; use to dispatch to the current recipe

recipe_trial.description: Dispatch a multi-parameter candidate batch without writing a recipe version. You may target the running recipe with only line_id or pass recipe_id explicitly. Permission model: bound recipe, secondary auth, and run gate; candidates may only cover parameters in the recipe. With a manual binding or manual line, the trial suspends for human approval — hypothesis is required (why this trial and on what evidence). The whole batch lands at once; after re-measurement, persist improvement with recipe_update or roll back with recipe_rollback(dispatch=true). Subject to the per-line trial interval (default >=5 minutes) and the four-layer limits.

recipe_id.description: Recipe id (mutually exclusive with line_id; explicit id wins)

params.description: Candidate parameters (>=1; include every change in one batch to avoid oscillation)

hypothesis.description: Trial hypothesis/rationale (required: knowledge-base entry or data analysis conclusion)

emergency.description: Emergency exemption from the recipe dispatch rate limit (does NOT skip approval; the card is marked [EMERGENCY] and still needs a human; abuse is audited)

line_id.description: Line id (mutually exclusive with recipe_id): resolve the active recipe

recipe_rollback.description: Roll recipe parameters back to a stable version (a historical version or the last good batch) by creating a new non-destructive version; with dispatch=true it also restores the parameters to the line as a batch. Permission model: bound recipe, secondary auth, and run gate; manual bindings suspend for HITL — reason is required (e.g. optimization degradation/out-of-limit).

version.description: Roll back to this historical version (either version or to_last_good)

to_last_good.description: true = restore the last good batch parameters

dispatch.description: true = restore the definition AND re-dispatch parameters to the PLC (use when the optimization loop degrades); default false = definition only

emergency.description: Emergency exemption from the recipe dispatch rate limit (does NOT skip approval; still needs a human; abuse is audited)

recipe_log.description: Query recipe change history (create/update/trial/apply/per-parameter ACK/approval/optimization window verdict/rollback/start-batch dispatch; newest first). Returns only scope=line records, each with line and recipe attribution. Pass recipe_id to get the whole event family across kinds (including kind=write dispatch ACKs); line.start/line.stop are included (starting a line dispatches recipe parameters). Without line_id the channel-bound line is used; recipe_id narrows to that recipe's line. Time via from/to or minutes. Use dcw_journal for per-node write history.

line_id.description: Line id (must be readable; default: channel-bound line, or all readable lines when unbound)

recipe_id.description: Filter by recipe id (implies its line)

product_id.description: Filter by product id (must belong to a readable line)

to.description: Window end (ISO; must be after from)

minutes.description: Lookback minutes when from is omitted (default 1440 = 24h)

recipe_versions.description: View the parameter version history of a recipe (old to new): version, time, source (user/agent/system), actor name, change reason, and parameter diff. Use it to confirm a target version before rollback and to review who changed what and why. Visibility = recipe line readable (node-granted line ∪ bound recipe line ∪ channel-bound line). Rollback goes through recipe_rollback (write gate; manual bindings need HITL).

limit.description: Return the latest N versions (default 20, max 50)

mes_fetch.description: Fetch data from MES REST points (code-enforced guards: only your bound DCW points; window <=7 days; <=5000 rows; <=6 fetches per 60 seconds). Formats are auto-detected: scalar/vector (thickness profile)/image frame (CCD, persisted automatically)/table/event stream. Responses include field-level dictionaries; with include_data=true, sampled rows carry actual arrays (field names, labels, units, ranges, physical meaning; vector fields also list per-point meaning) so the Agent can reason on meaning, not bare numbers. If no dictionary exists it says so explicitly — do not guess units. Three modes: no from/to = current snapshot; from/to and max_rows<=2000 = synchronous inline; max_rows>2000 = asynchronous CSV dataset plus a same-name *.manifest.json (dictionary/units/ranges/batch attribution), returning job_id/dataset_id. Use mes_export for full raw offline analysis.

ids.description: Target point id array (ids from mes_catalog; must be your bound DCW points)

from.description: Window start ISO time (paired with to; omit both for a current snapshot)

to.description: Window end ISO time (paired with from; window <=7 days)

max_rows.description: Row cap (default 500, hard cap 5000; >2000 goes to an async dataset)

param.description: Business parameters passed through to the point data hook (e.g. {"lane":12,"agg":"mean"}); omit for points without a hook

include_data.description: Include actual sampled values/arrays in inline/snapshot responses (vectors show up to 64 points with labels; default false = statistics only)

mes_catalog.description: Search the MES REST point catalog (DCW points with driver=mes-rest). Each entry includes id/name/line/unit/range, capability flags (read/write/history/hook), point description, and the field-level data dictionary (field names/labels/units/ranges/vector point count; from the MES response dictionaryPath or node driverConfig.dictionary, cached after the first mes_fetch). This is the addressing entry for mes_fetch/mes_export; supports keyword (q) and line_id filters. Read-only catalog, never touches the device. Visibility = your bound DCW points plus parameter points inside your bound recipes.

q.description: Keyword substring filter (point name and description)

product_id.description: Narrow to the product's line (rejected if it conflicts with line_id)

recipe_id.description: Narrow to the recipe's line (rejected if it conflicts with line_id)

line_context.description: Read the full picture of the lines/products/recipes you control (read before acting): line scenario description, run state and active batch, product description, active recipe (name/version/description) with per-parameter target vs PLC value vs process window (plus parameter key and description), your bound nodes and recipes (running/not running), and known good batches; when no batch is active, the line's recipe definitions are listed. Visibility = node-granted line ∪ bound recipe line ∪ channel-bound line (read-only). Confirm ownership and state before using recipe_* tools. [Value semantics: value = platform setpoint, readValue = PLC measured feedback; they may differ briefly during hold/heartbeat windows or disconnections — state which one you cite.]

line_id.description: Restrict to a line id (must be a line of your bound nodes; default: all lines you own)

my_industrial_nodes.description: List all your industrial bindings and semantic cards — one card per DCW node (PLC/MES point) and DAQ node: physical quantity/unit/range/precision, process semantics (mechanism and tuning rules), safe range and active-recipe process window, current setpoint, dispatch path (PLC driver or MES writeHook single field), per-step cap and operating rules; plus the recipe operation surface for your bound recipes (run state/binding mode manual=per-action HITL or auto/ secondary auth state/parameter table with keys and descriptions). Call this before any industrial operation. Binding prerequisites: daq/dcw bindings for nodes, recipe bindings for recipes — unbound objects never appear.

optimizer_solve.description: Solve one optimization problem under your binding authorization (numeric backends: SciPy/OSQP), returning a candidate MV trajectory and first-step suggestion. The channel must be bound to an optimizer profile; with multiple bindings pass binding_id explicitly. Missing optimization eligibility returns a locatable gap instead of fabricating a plan. Recommendations do not grant device write permission.

binding_id.description: Binding id (required with multiple bindings; optional when unique)

optimizer_status.description: Read the terminal state, candidates, and recommendation status of an optimization run (read-only). The run must belong to the current agent's binding; cross-agent queries return BINDING_NOT_OWNED.
